L0@P0: Finding All Maximally-Matchable Edges in a Bipartite Graph
L1@P0: Tamir Tassa∗
L2@P0: Abstract
L3@P0: We consider the problem of finding all maximally-matchable edges in a bipartite graph G =
L4@P0: (V, E), i.e., all edges that are included in some maximum matching. We show that given any maximum matching in the graph, it is possible to perform this computation in linear time O(n + m)
L5@P0: (where n = |V | and m = |E|). Hence, the time complexity of finding all maximally-matchable
L6@P0: edges reduces to that of finding a single maximum matching, which is O(n
L7@P0: 1/2m) (Hopcroft and
L8@P0: Karp [12]), or O((n/ log n)
L9@P0: 1/2m) for dense graphs with m = Θ(n2

L11@P0: complexity improves upon that of the best known algorithms for the problem, which is O(nm)
L12@P0: (Costa [5] for bipartite graphs, and Carvalho and Cheriyan [6] for general graphs). Other algorithms for solving that problem are randomized algorithms due to Rabin and Vazirani [15] and
L13@P0: Cheriyan [3], the runtime of which is O˜(n
L14@P0: 2.376). Our algorithm, apart from being deterministic,
L15@P0: improves upon that time complexity for bipartite graphs when m = O(n
L16@P0: r
L17@P0: ) and r < 1.876. In
L18@P0: addition, our algorithm is elementary, conceptually simple, and easy to implement.
L19@P0: Keywords. Bipartite graphs, perfect matchings, maximum matchings, maximally-matchable edges
L20@P0: 1 Introduction
L21@P0: Let V1 be a set of men and V2 be a set of women that are registered in a matchmaking agency.
L22@P0: Each of the men (women) has an associated description and given preferences regarding the woman
L23@P0: (man) with whom he (she) wishes to get acquainted. Those descriptions and preferences induce a
L24@P0: bipartite graph G of compatibilities on the set of nodes V = V1∪V2. The agency then presents to the
L25@P0: clients the links that are relevant to them, so that they can choose whom to meet. Some of those links
L26@P0: may not be extended to a maximum matching in the bipartite graph. The agency has an incentive to
L27@P0: identify those links upfront and not offer them to its clients, since if they would be offered and one
L28@P0: of them would be successful, it would prevent the possibility of achieving a maximum matching.
L29@P0: Therefore, given the full bipartite graph G, it is necessary to remove from it all edges that are not
L30@P0: part of a maximum matching, or, alternatively speaking, it is needed to compute the subgraph of G
L31@P0: that equals the union of all maximum matchings in G.
L32@P0: In order to formalize this problem, we recall some of the basic terminology regarding matchings
L33@P0: in graphs.

L36@P0-1: 1Definition 1.1. Let G = (V, E) be a graph.
L37@P1: • A matching in G is a collection M ⊆ E of non-adjacent edges.
L38@P1: • A matching M is called maximal if it is not a proper subset of any other matching.
L39@P1: • A maximal matching M is called a maximum (cardinality) matching if there does not exist a
L40@P1: matching with a greater cardinality.
L41@P1: • A maximum matching M is called perfect if it covers all of the nodes in V .
L42@P1: • An edge e ∈ E is a maximally-matchable edge if it is included in some maximum matching.1
L43@P1: We study here one of the fundamental problems in matching theory, namely, the identification
L44@P1: of all maximally-matchable edges in a given graph G. We focus here on bipartite graphs, i.e.
L45@P1: G = (V, E) where V = V1 ∪ V2, V1 ∩ V2 = ∅, and E ⊆ V1 × V2, and devise an efficient algorithm
L46@P1: for that problem in such graphs.
L47@P1: Our main contributions herein are summarized as follows: In case we are given one of the maximum matchings in the bipartite graph G = (V, E), Algorithm 3 in Section 2 finds all maximallymatchable edges in linear time O(n + m), where n = |V | and m = |E|. (In the application that
L48@P1: motivated this study there was indeed one “natural” maximum matching that was known without
L49@P1: any computation, see Section 5.) Without such prior knowledge on the graph, we may first find
L50@P1: any maximum matching in the graph, and then proceed to apply Algorithm 3 in order to complete
L51@P1: the computation in additional linear time. Algorithm 1 implements this approach. Its runtime is
L52@P1: dominated by the runtime of the procedure for finding a maximum matching.
L53@P1: Algorithm 1 Finding all maximally-matchable edges in a bipartite graph G = (V, E).
L54@P1: Input: A bipartite graph G = (V, E).
L55@P1: Output: All maximally-matchable edges in E.

L57@P1: 2: Using M, invoke Algorithm 3 in order to find all maximally-matchable edges in G.

L7@P0: 摘 要： 针对空间信息网络中大量移动用户跨域认证问题，提出了一种基于动态撤销机制的安全高效的批量认
L8@P0: 证方案。所提方案通过对卫星行动轨迹的预测以及实时更新会话密钥，达到提前完成密钥协商的作用。同时，还
L9@P0: 设计了可供单个以及大量移动终端进行签名并验证的算法，有效减轻了卫星的计算负担，结合布谷鸟过滤器实现
L10@P0: 了移动终端动态撤销和恶意接入控制的功能。最后，在 Diffie-Hellman 假设下，基于随机预言机模型和自动化验
L11@P0: 证工具证明了所提方案可以抵抗重放以及中间人等攻击；方案实现了可追踪性、可撤销性等安全目标，与现有最
L12@P0: 优方案相比，传输和计算效率分别提高了 80%和 20%以上。
L13@P0: 关键词：空间信息网络；密钥协商；动态撤销；批量认证；自动化验证工具

L25@P0: Abstract: A secure and efficient batch authentication scheme based on dynamic revocation mechanism was proposed for
L26@P0: the problem of cross-domain authentication of a large number of mobile users in space information networks. Early key
L27@P0: negotiation was achieved by predicting the satellite trajectory and updating the session key in real time. Algorithms were
L28@P0: designed for a single as well as a large number of mobile terminals to perform signing and verification, which effectively
L29@P0: reduce the computational burden of satellites. Cuckoo filters were adopted by the new scheme to achieve dynamic revocation and malicious access control of mobile terminals. Finally, under the Diffie-Hellman assumption, the proposed
L30@P0: scheme was proved to be resistant to replay and man-in-the-middle attacks based on a random oracle model and automated validation of internet security protocols and applications. Security goals such as traceability and revocability were
L31@P0: achieved by the scheme, thus improving the efficiency of transmission and computation by more than 80% and 20%, respectively, compared with the existing optimal scheme.
L32@P0: Keywords: space information network, key agreement, dynamic revocation, batch authentication, AVISPA

L102@P1: 针对上述问题，本文主要做出了以下贡献。

L106@P1: 户先从附近其他用户接收到所有签名信息，然后将
L107@P1: 其聚合为一个签名，这样卫星只需确认已注册移动

L111@P1: 计费的问题，因此所提方案加入了动态撤销机制。
L112@P1: 该机制通过引入布谷鸟过滤器，支持查询、插入和
